preamble: Method: Solve the clues and fit the solutions in the diagram wherever they will go.

clue.text: Trickster's admission of being tricked, making John see to Mike

parts.note: surface reading: a prankster owning up that a prank has backfired
setter's reading: a playful picture of one person being made the butt, the laugh landing on the speaker

explanation.surface: A prankster confesses to being caught out while getting John to look after Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is what a trickster says when a trick rebounds; the rest of the clue is Araucaria's whimsical scene of a prank that ends up landing on its maker.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom is the standard rueful confession when someone who set out to fool others has instead been fooled.

clue.text: Mixed race boy supplies football club teas

parts.note: Hal is a boy's name, short for Henry

indicators.note: read as 'supple' things, the letters are bent into a fresh order

parts.note: standard abbreviation, as in Arsenal FC
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A young lad of mixed background lays on the refreshments for a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: The term is dated and now considered offensive, but it is what the grid needs. Hal is a common crossword boy.
explanation.definitionFit: An older adjective, now offensive, describing a person whose parents come from different ethnic backgrounds.

clue.text: Smoked food?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rolled cannabis cigarette, something that gets smoked
second meaning: a large cut of meat for roasting

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about kippers or bacon, but splits into two senses of one word; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasting cut of meat is food, while slang for a hand-rolled marijuana cigarette names something people smoke.

clue.text: Cooker about to return humble greeting

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters run backwards
to be about something is to surround it on all sides

parts.note: a wok is a Chinese cooking pan
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook greets someone meekly before heading back.
explanation.walkthrough: The container is built first and only then turned round, so the pan's letters end up at both ends. KOTOW is a variant spelling of kowtow.
explanation.definitionFit: Kowtowing, kneeling and touching the forehead to the ground, was a deeply deferential Chinese form of salutation.

clue.text: Popular opening or select opening for patentees

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a vent is an opening or outlet
taken as written

indicators.note: an opening is the start of something, so only the initial letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A choice of public or exclusive launch events for people holding patents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' appears twice doing two jobs: first as a synonym for a gap, then as the signal to take a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: People granted patents are typically those who devised new machines or processes, the originators of those designs.

clue.text: Coleridge's narrator made ten dollars

indicators.note: making something means forming it from raw material into a new shape

parts.note: 10 written as the figures one and zero, looking like I and O
taken as written

explanation.surface: The storyteller in a Coleridge poem earned a modest ten dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten is turned into the look-alike letters IO, a common crossword trick with digits.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner is told by an aged seaman, so an ancient mariner is an elderly seafarer.

clue.text: Piece of music encountered outside books

indicators.note: one thing sitting outside another wraps around it

parts.note: met means came across
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A tune heard while standing outside some books, perhaps outside a library.
explanation.walkthrough: OT for Old Testament (and NT for New) is the standard crossword way to clue 'books'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short choral composition, usually sacred and unaccompanied, is a specific type of musical work.

clue.text: Equation: solution (if Roman and atomic numbers) Z = F

parts.words: Equation: solution (if Roman and atomic numbers) Z = F
parts.note: surface reading: a piece of algebra with its solution set out

parts.words: (if Roman and atomic numbers) Z = F
parts.note: setter's reading: X as a Roman numeral is ten and Y has atomic number 39, so the third letter stands for forty-nine, the entry beginning with F

explanation.surface: A maths problem with its working shown and a final value given.
explanation.walkthrough: X is 10 in Roman numerals and Y is yttrium, element 39; their sum is 49, the answer to the F clue (FORTY-NINE) elsewhere in this grid.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the simplest textbook algebraic sum, an equality statement relating three unknown quantities.

clue.text: Walkover here? If with donkey, remove all but centre of part 2

parts.note: surface reading: an easy win; setter's reading: a place where pedestrians walk over the road

parts.words: If with donkey, remove all but centre of part 2
parts.note: a striped animal crossed with a donkey is a zebrass: keep only the middle two letters of the second word and you get that hybrid

explanation.surface: Asking where a one-sided contest took place, with a puzzling instruction about a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: A zebra crossing is the British term for a striped pedestrian crossing. The second half is a joke: crossing a zebra with a donkey gives a zebrass, which is ZEBRA plus the central SS of CROSSING.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrians walk over the road at this striped marked point, so it is literally a place for walking over.

clue.text: Friend with spray to work on the hand?

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a mist is a fine spray

explanation.surface: A friend reaches for a spray, perhaps a moisturiser, to treat someone's hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic description of the answer as a noun: someone whose job is working on the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune teller who reads the lines of the palm earns a living by studying people's hands.

clue.text: Patrol boat (see minieditor?)

parts.note: v. abbreviates Latin vide, meaning see
ED for editor plus the diminutive ending -ETTE, as in kitchenette, makes a mini one

explanation.surface: A naval patrol vessel, with a bracketed cross-reference as if to a small editor.
explanation.walkthrough: The coinage 'minieditor' is the joke: -ette is a suffix that makes things small, so a little editor is an ED-ETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vedette was a small fast naval craft used for scouting and picket duty, essentially a mounted sentry afloat.

clue.text: Full length hook with next to last letter

indicators.note: the final letter gives way to its neighbour further along the alphabet

parts.note: uncus is Latin for a hook, also used in anatomy for hooked structures

explanation.surface: A full-length line ending in a hook, then the penultimate letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Next to last letter' looks like Y, the penultimate letter of the alphabet; instead it means swap the last letter of the hook word, S, for the letter next to it, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or book released without any edits or cuts is presented at its complete original length.

clue.text: Pursued and succeeded

definitions.meaning: second meaning: followed someone in sequence, came next

explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeded' tempts as 'triumphed', but here it means followed, as one monarch succeeds another.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both chasing a quarry and following a predecessor in time or office.

clue.text: You suffer a bit, said Joe in Arabic

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so it is the sound of the words that counts

parts.note: only a bit of the phrase is used, cutting the last syllable

explanation.surface: Someone sympathises with a sufferer, then translates a name into Arabic.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'you suff(er)' with the end chopped off and you hear the Arabic name. Joe is short for Joseph, whose Arabic form is Yusuf.
explanation.definitionFit: Yusuf is the Arabic form of Joseph, and Joe is the familiar short form of that same biblical name.

clue.text: Square for river that's kept in

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something kept in is held inside an enclosure

parts.note: the Tyne is the river of Newcastle in north-east England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A town square named for a river, with something kept inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does double duty in the surface but here it is the very letters held inside the river. It is also the Z of 8 down: 10 + 39.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven times seven makes this number, so it is a perfect square in the arithmetic sense.

clue.text: Sophist is smart about work record

indicators.note: being about something means going round it

parts.note: chic means stylish or smart
op. is the abbreviation for opus, a work
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A clever arguer is described as sharp regarding someone's employment history.
explanation.walkthrough: Op., short for opus, is the usual crossword 'work'. A sophist is a specious arguer, and chop-logic is an old word for exactly such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A chop-logic, in older usage, is a person who argues over petty distinctions, much as a sophist uses specious reasoning.

clue.text: Trickster holding greater part of culture grower

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within your grasp

parts.note: a cheat is a trickster
most is the greater part of anything

explanation.surface: A con artist clutching most of some cultivated crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Culture' here is the laboratory sense, a population of bacteria, not the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: This lab apparatus keeps a bacterial population growing steadily by continually feeding fresh medium in at a fixed rate.

clue.text: Actor's part in gallery near to being clean?

indicators.note: a thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: the gods is the highest theatre gallery
an actor's lines are the speech they must learn

explanation.surface: A performer's role played up in the cheap seats, while worrying about being nearly clean.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'Cleanliness is next to godliness', turning it round so the answer is what sits beside being clean.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb places piety right beside cleanliness, so devoutness is jokingly what lies 'next to' being clean.

clue.text: Queen's (ER's) show rum quality

indicators.note: a show is a display put on, here a new arrangement put on for display

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A royal show of Her Majesty's own, with a hint of oddness.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen, so the bracket looks like a gloss; it is extra letters to mix in. Rum is British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum in British slang means odd or strange, and queer in its older sense also means peculiar, so the noun is oddness.

clue.text: Took no part in the cowboy show?

parts.note: took a ride, as in took the bus
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone sat out the cowboy display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took no part' reads as an idiom for abstaining; split it and the first word becomes a past tense of riding, apt for a broncobuster.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a public exhibition of cowboy skills like bronco riding and roping cattle.

clue.text: Beatles' address to Turk in foreign parts

indicators.note: placed in something means set inside it

parts.note: abroad means in foreign parts
a bey was a Turkish governor or title of rank

explanation.surface: The Beatles send a message to a Turkish man living overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests a speech, but it is a street address: the London road where the Beatles recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles' recording studios stood on this London street, which also titled their famous album with the zebra crossing cover.

clue.text: Relative to Pole, unknown in New York

definitions.note: a place in New York rather than a phrase meaning 'in'

parts.note: bro is short for brother
N for the North Pole
X is the standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A Polish relative whose whereabouts in New York are unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' with its capital looks like a Polish person; it is a magnetic pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bronx is one of the five boroughs of New York City, so it is a district found there.

clue.text: Capital letter missing from scene of oracle

indicators.note: something missing from a whole has been taken away

parts.note: Delphi in Greece was home to the famous oracle of Apollo
one letter, which turns out to be P

explanation.surface: A capital letter has disappeared from where an ancient oracle stood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital letter' reads as an upper-case letter; 'Capital' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi, more precisely New Delhi within it, is the seat of India's national government.

clue.text: They are hard on the hand

definitions.text: They are hard on the hand

parts.words: They are hard on the hand
parts.note: surface reading: things that are rough or harsh on your hands, like heavy work

parts.words: They are hard on the hand
parts.note: setter's reading: tough things that literally sit on the fingers, and are proverbially hard

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard on' means harsh to, but here it is literal: hard things located on the hand, and 'hard as nails' seals it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fingernails are tough keratin plates growing at the tips of the fingers, and the idiom says something tough is 'hard as' them.

clue.text: Roman family name for women only?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the clan name, the middle of a Roman's three names
second meaning, split into two words: no males admitted

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: split the Latin term into two English words and it describes a ladies-only space. In Gaius Julius Caesar, Julius is that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Romans had praenomen, nomen and cognomen; the middle one identified the gens, or clan, and so works as a surname.

clue.text: Duns' advocate is confined by great man

indicators.note: something confined is shut inside a boundary

parts.note: Scott, the Antarctic explorer or Sir Walter the novelist, a famous figure
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawyer in the Scottish town of Duns is hemmed in by a towering figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Duns is a Scottish town, but here it is Duns Scotus, the medieval theologian. 'Great man' is vague; the explorer or novelist Scott fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the scholastic philosopher John Duns Scotus champions his doctrines, hence an advocate of Duns.

clue.text: Strike by Pole which can draw blood

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
per means by, as in per post
N for the North Pole

explanation.surface: A blow from a Polish man that might make someone bleed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: the creature latches on to fish and sucks blood.
explanation.definitionFit: The lampern, or river lamprey, is a jawless fish that attaches to other fish with a sucker mouth and feeds on their blood.

clue.text: Spurious pretext is news that should stand up in court

definitions.text: that should stand up in court

indicators.note: something spurious is false, not the genuine article, so the letters are not in their true order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fake excuse is presented as news that should hold up in a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand up in court' sounds like evidence holding up; it is literal, a person who stands in the witness box.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist called to give professional opinion evidence in a trial testifies from the witness box, standing before the court.
